images.title: Each fold doubles the thickness
images.purpose: Shows a sheet 0.001 cm thick becoming 0.002, 0.004 and 0.008 cm as it is folded once, twice and three times.
images.composition: Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no people, no extra text. Four paper stacks stand on one baseline in a row from left to right, each taller than the one before, with a curved arrow between neighbouring stacks.
images.exact_structure: Four stacks of identical thin flat teal (#0072B2) rectangles (paper layers), bottoms on one shared grey baseline, evenly spaced from left to right. Stack 1 has 1 layer, stack 2 has 2 layers, stack 3 has 4 layers, stack 4 has 8 layers; every layer has the same width and the same height, so stack 4 is exactly 8 times as tall as stack 1. Under the stacks, in order, the labels '0.001 cm', '0.002 cm', '0.004 cm', '0.008 cm'. Above the gaps between stacks are exactly 3 curved amber (#E69F00) arrows, each going from one stack to the next, each labelled '× 2'. Exactly 4 stacks, 15 layers in all, 3 arrows.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Every fold multiplies the thickness by 2.
images.description: Shows a sheet 0.001 cm thick becoming 0.002, 0.004 and 0.008 cm as it is folded once, twice and three times.
images.context: 0.001 × 2 = 0.002, 0.002 × 2 = 0.004, 0.004 × 2 = 0.008; the table continues to 1.024 cm after 10 folds and about 131 cm after 17.
images.teaching_notes: The label '× 2' appears 3 times, once on each arrow. Ask how many layers stack 5 would have.

image_decisions.why: Seeing the layers double from 1 to 2 to 4 to 8 is the whole idea of this concept: each fold multiplies the thickness by 2.
